text:
Sam: Heads-up — aligning Q1 perf priorities. Acme + Beta have in-flight asks. We need to choose what to prioritize: kernel optimizations, quantization pipeline, or KV/prefix cache + batching. Quick thoughts?

Priya: +1. Acme's main pain is p95 generation latency ~320ms on 8k tokens; they want <200ms. Our p50 is ~90ms. Quant (4-bit) saves ~30-40% cost but we see ~10-15% quality regressions on long-context prompts.

Marco: Data point from experiments last week: switching to the new f16 matmul kernel gave ~20% perf on larger decoding workloads but regressed smaller/edge-case models. We can gate kernels by model-tags.

Jess: Can we get quick wins with KV cache improvements + smarter eviction? That should hit tail latency and memory pressure without touching kernels. Customers tend to accept that faster.

Sam: I'm leaning to low-risk high-impact first: KV cache + batching. But we must define concrete launch criteria and rollback plan.

Lin: Proposed launch checklist:
- latency target: p95 < 250ms on our standard perf-suite
- throughput: >= 800 req/s on reserved 4xA100 profile (steady-state)
- regression evals: delta on our prompt-set (quality) < 0.5%
- canary rollout strategy: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48-72h windows
- monitoring: alert when error-rate increases > 0.5% or latency spikes 2x baseline
- cost checks: measure per-token cost delta within 24h

Priya: Add security/compliance check: model pinning must be available for enterprise customers + KMS integration verified.

Sam: Good. Trade-offs: kernels = biggest uplift but highest QA/compat risk. Quantization = infrastructure work (buildpack, storage for quant weights, conversion pipeline) and subtle quality regressions we must catch. KV cache + batching = low-hanging fruit but smaller upside.

Marco: Customer ask prioritization: Acme = latency, Beta = cost, Gamma = both. Proposed split: Q1a = KV cache + batching + default perf dashboards; Q1b = gated kernel rollout for top models; Q1c = start quant infra for opt-in models.

Jess: Rough timelines from eng estimates: KV+batching = 3 sprints (including QA/runbook), kernel opt-in canary = 4 sprints (benchmarks + tests), quant infra + conversion tooling = 6 sprints.

Sam: Owners suggestion: Priya -> KV/cache & batching, Marco -> kernel opt-ins, Lin -> quant infra. OKRs to propose: reduce hosted p95 by 30% for top-5 served models; reduce per-token cost by 15% on opt-in quant models; maintain quality regressions below threshold.

Priya: I'll draft a short PRD + rollout playbook. Will include: perf targets, smoke tests, canary gates, rollback steps, customer comms. Who wants to co-author?

Marco: I'll own the kernel test harness + perf infra updates and add regression suites.

Jess: I'll create observability dashboards and a runbook for incidents + rollback triggers.

Sam: Quick snippet for bench command we'll use in perf infra:
```bash
# run decode benchmark for 8k seq on candidate build
run-bench --model gpt-like --seq-len 8192 --profile reserved-4xA100 --p95 --throughput
```

Lin: For quant pipeline we need to standardize a conversion manifest. Example config snippet:
```json
{"model": "redwood/gptx", "quant": "4bit", "calibrate": true}
```

ops-bot: Deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance window: kernel canary runway 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Please confirm owners and blackout windows.

Sam: Sounds good. Next steps: commit to KV/batching first. Priya will share PRD by EOD Monday. Marco to start kernel canary plan; Lin to scope quant infra. Sync Wed 10am to finalize Q1 plan. :thumbsup:

Priya: ack — drafting PRD now, will @Sam/Marco/Jess for review.

Marco: will sync perf benchmarks and push initial results by Tuesday.

Jess: will stub dashboards and add alert thresholds; will link when ready.

Sam: Thanks all — short but concrete. We'll track as an initiative in the quarterly roadmap board and tie to the OKRs above. :rocket:
